tldr: Meta Connect on Sep 24 put Muse glasses, voice and video at the center of Meta's hardware push. Three weeks later, the competitive and privacy questions around AI glasses started to surface.
whats_new: Meta extended Private Processing to its AI glasses on Oct 14, running AI workloads in confidential VMs and TEEs with remote attestation; Alibaba's Qwen glasses launched the same day as a rival.
why_it_matters: Always-on camera glasses send sensor data to cloud models, so the trust boundary matters. Meta's attested TEE design is a reference pattern for any team shipping on-device-plus-cloud AI.

status.detail: Meta's glasses line now has a published privacy architecture and its first named competitor from Alibaba.

beats.headline: Meta Connect 2026 unveils Muse glasses, voice, video and Charm
Private Processing arrives on glasses as Alibaba's Qwen glasses enter the market
beats.summary: Meta publishes its confidential-computing design; Alibaba positions its Qwen glasses against Meta's eyewear.

open_questions: Will Meta publish an independent audit or attestation verifier for glasses Private Processing?
Will Meta or third parties open the glasses to developer-built agents?
take_for_builders: If you send wearable or camera data to cloud models, compare your pipeline with Meta's design: TEE-based processing, remote attestation, anonymous credentials and OHTTP routing.
